title: Krishna Questions the Indra Sacrifice
one_line_summary: Krishna, bowing humbly, asks Nanda and the elders what ceremony they have begun, its fruit, for whom, and by what means it is accomplished.
source_excerpt: Krishna, bowing humbly, asked the elders led by Nanda: 'Tell me, father, what is this ceremony you have undertaken? What is its fruit, for whom, and by what means is the sacrifice accomplished?' (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 2)

title: Nanda Explains the Indra Worship
one_line_summary: Nanda explains that Indra, lord of rain, is worshipped with offerings produced by his own showers.
source_excerpt: Nanda replied: 'Indra is the lord of the clouds, and by his showers all beings are nourished; we and other men worship him with offerings made of the things his rain produces.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 7-8)

title: Krishna Argues for Worshipping Govardhana
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Nanda the cowherds should worship Govardhana hill, the cows and the brahmins rather than Indra.
source_excerpt: Krishna, to break Indra's pride, argued that beings are born and perish by their own karma, that the cowherds' living is cattle and forest, and so the sacrifice should be offered to Govardhana hill, the cows and the brahmins, not to Indra. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 12-24)

title: The Cowherds Worship Govardhana
one_line_summary: Nanda and the cowherds accept Krishna's words and perform the sacrifice to Govardhana hill.
source_excerpt: Nanda and the cowherds accepted Krishna's words and performed everything as he had said: they gave offerings to the hill, the cows and the brahmins, and with their cattle made circumambulation of Govardhana. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 30-32)

title: Krishna Receives Offerings as Govardhana
one_line_summary: Krishna takes a vast form declaring himself the hill, and eats the offerings while the people bow in wonder.
source_excerpt: Krishna, taking another form and declaring 'I am the hill,' ate the abundant offerings, and the people of Vraja, seeing the embodied hill, bowed to it, saying 'Behold, the hill has favored us.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 34-36)

title: Indra Becomes Furious
one_line_summary: Indra learns his worship has been stopped and grows angry with the cowherds whose lord is Krishna.
source_excerpt: When Indra learned that his own worship had been obstructed, he grew angry with the cowherds, Nanda and the rest, whose lord was Krishna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 38)

title: Indra Unleashes the Storm on Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Furious Indra sends the Samvartaka storm-clouds to destroy Nanda's gokula with torrent, hail and wind.
source_excerpt: Furious Indra set in motion the Samvartaka clouds of destruction, saying 'Scatter the pride of these cowherds, drive their cattle to destruction'; and the clouds, freed of restraint, tormented Nanda's gokula with torrents, lightning, thunder and hail. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

title: Krishna Lifts Govardhana Hill
one_line_summary: Krishna lifts Govardhana hill with one hand and holds it aloft like an umbrella to shelter the cowherds.
source_excerpt: Seeing the cowherds stricken by hail and wind, Krishna reasoned that Indra in anger was sending this out-of-season storm, and to destroy the pride of those who fancy themselves lords, he lifted Govardhana hill with one hand and held it up like an umbrella. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 13-18)

title: Seven Days Beneath Govardhana
one_line_summary: The cowherds shelter beneath the hill for seven days while Krishna holds it, until Indra relents.
source_excerpt: Krishna told the cowherds to enter the hollow beneath the hill with their cattle without fear, and he held the mountain for seven days without moving from his place; Indra, astonished, checked his clouds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 19-23)

title: Krishna Restores the Hill and the Cowherds Rejoice
one_line_summary: Krishna sets the hill back in place; Nanda, Yashoda and Balarama embrace him and the gods rain flowers.
source_excerpt: When the storm ceased the cowherds came out with their goods, and Krishna set the hill back in its place as before; Nanda, Yashoda, Rohini and Balarama embraced him, the gods rained flowers, and the gopis sang of his deeds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-32)

title: The Cowherds Marvel and Nanda Recounts Garga's Prophecy
one_line_summary: Astonished at Krishna's deeds, the cowherds wonder how a boy could do such things, and Nanda reassures them with Garga's words.
source_excerpt: The cowherds, astonished at Krishna's superhuman deeds, wondered how a seven-year-old boy could hold up a great mountain, and Nanda recounted to them the words of Garga, who had foretold that this child was Vasudeva, equal to Narayana, who would protect them from all dangers. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-16)
notes: Mostly a retrospective recap of earlier Vraja deeds; included for the doubt-to-reassurance frame.

title: Indra Surrenders and Begs Forgiveness
one_line_summary: Ashamed Indra approaches Krishna, touches his feet, and asks forgiveness for his pride.
source_excerpt: Indra, ashamed, approached Krishna in seclusion, touched his feet with his crown, and said: 'I, intoxicated by my sovereignty, have offended you, not knowing your power; forgive me, Lord, and may such evil intention never arise in me again.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-15)

title: Krishna Is Consecrated as Govinda
one_line_summary: Surabhi the divine cow praises Krishna, and Indra bathes and names him Govinda.
source_excerpt: Surabhi, the divine cow, praised Krishna, saying the gods, urged by Brahma, would consecrate him; then Indra, with the waters of the celestial Ganga, bathed Krishna and named him Govinda, and the gods, Gandharvas and Siddhas celebrated. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 20-22)

title: Nanda Is Seized by Varuna and Rescued
one_line_summary: A servant of Varuna seizes Nanda as he bathes at night; Krishna goes to Varuna's abode and frees him.
source_excerpt: While Nanda bathed in the Yamuna at night, a servant of Varuna seized him and carried him to Varuna's abode; Krishna, hearing the cowherds' cries, went there, and Varuna, honoring him, returned Nanda with apologies. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

title: Krishna Reveals His Supreme Abode
one_line_summary: Krishna shows the cowherds his own abode beyond darkness, the eternal Brahman-light.
source_excerpt: Nanda told his kinsmen of the wondrous honor shown by the lord of the waters; and Krishna, wishing to grant his people's desire, revealed to the cowherds his own abode beyond darkness, the eternal light of Brahman. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 9-15)

title: The Gopis Abandon Their Homes
one_line_summary: Krishna plays his flute on an autumn night and the gopis leave homes, husbands and duties to rush to him.
source_excerpt: Seeing the autumn nights, Krishna resolved to enjoy himself; he played his flute, and the gopis, their minds captured, left their homes, husbands, children and duties and hurried to him, heedless of all restraint. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-7)

title: Krishna Tests the Gopis
one_line_summary: Krishna tells the gopis to return to their husbands, and they plead that he is their very soul.
source_excerpt: Krishna first told the gopis to return to their husbands and children, speaking of the duty of women; but the gopis answered with tears that he was their very soul, and that having abandoned everything for his feet, they could not return. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 17-41)

title: Krishna Relents and Sports with the Gopis
one_line_summary: Krishna smiles, shows the gopis favor, and enjoys himself with them on the Yamuna's bank.
source_excerpt: Hearing their lament, Krishna, though self-satisfied, smilingly showed them favor and enjoyed himself with them on the sandy bank of the Yamuna, and the gopis thought themselves the most blessed of women. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 42-46)

title: Krishna Vanishes
one_line_summary: To quell the pride rising in the gopis, Krishna suddenly disappears.
source_excerpt: Seeing the pride that had arisen in the gopis from their good fortune, Krishna vanished then and there, to humble them and favor them. (rendered from Sanskrit, verse 47)

title: The Gopis Search the Forest
one_line_summary: The gopis wander the forest questioning the trees and plants about the vanished Krishna.
source_excerpt: When Krishna disappeared, the gopis searched for him like madwomen from wood to wood, questioning the trees and plants, 'Have you seen Nanda's son, who stole our hearts with his smiles?' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 3-4)

title: The Gopis Enact Krishna's Lilas
one_line_summary: In their frenzy the gopis imitate Krishna's childhood deeds, each playing a part.
source_excerpt: In their frenzy the gopis imitated Krishna's deeds: one played Putana and another the cart; one lifted her arm like Govardhana, and another declared 'I am Krishna, see my graceful gait.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-19)

title: The Favored Gopi's Pride and Krishna's Second Vanishing
one_line_summary: Finding footprints of Krishna and his chosen gopi, the gopis marvel; she grows proud, and Krishna vanishes again.
source_excerpt: Finding Krishna's footprints and those of the gopi he had taken aside, the gopis marveled at her fortune; that favored gopi, grown proud, asked Krishna to carry her, and when he took her on his shoulder he vanished again, and she repented. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-38)

title: Krishna Reappears Among the Gopis
one_line_summary: Krishna reappears smiling and the gopis rise as if their life had returned; their grief ends.
source_excerpt: Krishna then appeared among the gopis, smiling, and they all rose at once as if their very life had returned; each embraced him in her own way, and their grief of separation was dispelled. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-9)

title: Krishna Teaches About Love
one_line_summary: Krishna answers the gopis' question about why he loves those who love him, explaining the ways of love.
source_excerpt: When the gopis asked why he loves those who love him, Krishna explained the ways of love, and told them their love for him, which had severed the bonds of home, could never be repaid, but that it returned to them of itself. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 15-21)

title: The Great Rasa Dance
one_line_summary: Krishna multiplies himself to dance between every gopi in the moonlit rasa; the gods watch and rain flowers.
source_excerpt: There Govinda began the rasa dance with the gopis, multiplying himself to stand between every pair; the gods rained flowers, the celestial women watching were bewildered, and Krishna sported with them through the moonlit autumn nights. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-24)
notes: Parikshit's subsequent question and Shuka's defence (33.25-38) are doctrinal and excluded.

title: Nanda Is Swallowed by a Serpent and Freed
one_line_summary: A great serpent swallows Nanda as he sleeps; Krishna's touch frees the cursed Vidyadhara Sudarshana.
source_excerpt: As the cowherds slept in Ambika's forest, a great hungry serpent swallowed Nanda; the cowherds struck it with firebrands in vain, but when Krishna touched it with his foot it became Sudarshana the Vidyadhara, freed from a sage's curse, and Nanda was released. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 4-17)

title: Shankhachuda Abducts the Gopis
one_line_summary: As Krishna and Balarama sing in the forest, the demon Shankhachuda carries off the gopis.
source_excerpt: As Krishna and Balarama sang in the forest at night among the gopis, the demon Shankhachuda, servant of Kubera, carried off the women, who cried 'Krishna! Rama!'; and the two brothers pursued him like two lions. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 24-27)

title: Krishna Slays Shankhachuda and Takes the Jewel
one_line_summary: Krishna overtakes the demon, strikes him dead and gives the crest-jewel to Balarama.
source_excerpt: Krishna overtook the fleeing demon, struck his head with his fist and took the bright jewel from his crest, and gave it to his elder brother Balarama while the women looked on. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 29-31)

title: Krishna Slays the Arishta Bull Demon
one_line_summary: The bull-demon Arishta terrorizes Vrindavan until Krishna seizes and slays him.
source_excerpt: The bull-demon Arishta, terrifying the cowherds and cattle, charged at Krishna, who seized him by the horns, flung him aside, threw him down and slew him; and the gods praised Krishna with showers of flowers. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-14)

title: Narada Reveals the Truth to Kamsa
one_line_summary: Narada tells Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama are the sons of Devaki and Rohini; Kamsa binds Vasudeva and Devaki.
source_excerpt: Narada came and told Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama were the sons of Devaki and Rohini, whom the frightened Vasudeva had entrusted to Nanda; hearing this, Kamsa seized his sword and bound Vasudeva and Devaki in iron fetters. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 15-18)

title: Kamsa Conspires with His Wrestlers
one_line_summary: Kamsa summons Chanura and Mushtika and orders Krishna and Balarama killed by wrestling and by the elephant Kuvalayapida.
source_excerpt: Kamsa summoned Chanura, Mushtika and his other wrestlers and ministers, and ordered that Krishna and Balarama be brought to Mathura to be killed in a wrestling match, with the elephant Kuvalayapida set at the arena gate to slay them. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 19-25)

title: Kamsa Sends Akrura to Fetch Krishna
one_line_summary: Kamsa, taking Akrura by the hand, sends him with sweet words to bring Krishna and Balarama to Mathura.
source_excerpt: Kamsa, taking Akrura by the hand, sent him with sweet words to bring Krishna and Balarama from Vraja, saying the bow sacrifice was to be seen; and Akrura, though he knew Kamsa's intent, agreed to carry out the command. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 26-39)

title: Krishna Slays the Keshi Horse Demon
one_line_summary: The horse-demon Keshi attacks, and Krishna thrusts his arm into its mouth until it chokes and dies.
source_excerpt: The horse-demon Keshi, sent by Kamsa, terrified the cowherds, but Krishna thrust his arm into the demon's open mouth and expanded it until Keshi, choked, fell dead, and the gods showered flowers on Krishna. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-7)

title: Krishna Slays the Vyoma Demon
one_line_summary: The demon Vyoma, disguised as a cowherd, carries off boys and seals them in a cave; Krishna slays him and frees them.
source_excerpt: As the cowherd boys played at thieves and keepers, the demon Vyoma, son of Maya, carried off many of them in a cowherd's disguise and sealed them in a mountain cave; Krishna seized and slew him and freed the boys. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 25-32)

title: Akrura Journeys to Vrindavan
one_line_summary: On the road Akrura, filled with devotion, ponders what merit has earned him the sight of Krishna.
source_excerpt: On the road Akrura, filled with devotion, pondered what merit had earned him the sight of Krishna, and he arrived at Gokula at sunset, gazing at the footprints of the Lord marked with the lotus and other signs. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-23)
notes: Largely devotional meditation during the journey.

title: Akrura Is Welcomed in Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Akrura sees Krishna and Balarama, prostrates, and is honored by Nanda with food and questions.
source_excerpt: Akrura saw Krishna and Balarama among the milking cows, fell at their feet, and was embraced; Nanda received him with food and honor, and asked how the Yadavas fared under the cruel Kamsa. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 33-42)

title: Akrura Reveals Kamsa's Plan
one_line_summary: Krishna questions Akrura, who tells him of Kamsa's enmity and the purpose of his mission.
source_excerpt: Krishna asked Akrura the news, and Akrura told him everything: Kamsa's enmity toward the Yadavas, his resolve to kill Vasudeva, and the reason he himself had been sent as messenger. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 3-8)

title: The Gopis Grieve at Krishna's Departure
one_line_summary: When Nanda proclaims the journey to Mathura, the gopis lament that Akrura is taking Krishna away.
source_excerpt: When Nanda proclaimed that they would go to Mathura, the gopis were stricken with grief, and they lamented, saying that Akrura, whose name means 'not cruel,' was cruel indeed to take Krishna away. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 12-30)

title: Krishna Consoles the Gopis
one_line_summary: As the chariot leaves, Krishna promises the weeping gopis that he will return.
source_excerpt: The gopis wept and followed the departing chariot, and Krishna consoled them with messages, saying 'I will come back'; and they returned, singing of his deeds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 31-36)

title: Akrura Beholds Krishna's Divine Vision
one_line_summary: Diving in the Yamuna, Akrura sees Krishna and Balarama as the Lord resting on Shesha surrounded by gods.
source_excerpt: At the Yamuna, Akrura bathed and, diving, beheld Krishna and Balarama there as the Lord resting on Shesha, surrounded by the hosts of gods; and he rose and praised him. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 37-56)

title: Krishna Withdraws the Vision and Akrura Reports to Kamsa
one_line_summary: Krishna withdraws the divine vision; Akrura drives on and reports to Kamsa before going home.
source_excerpt: Krishna withdrew the vision as an actor withdraws a play; Akrura, wondering, drove on, and after Krishna bade him go ahead, he entered Mathura, reported to Kamsa, and went to his own house. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-18)

title: Krishna and Balarama Enter Mathura
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama enter Mathura with the cowherds, and the city's women throng to see them.
source_excerpt: In the afternoon Krishna and Balarama entered Mathura with the cowherds, and the women of the city thronged to see them, forgetting their dress and work, and the brahmins honored them with curd, rice and garlands. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 18-30)

title: The Washerman's Insult and Death
one_line_summary: The king's washerman refuses Krishna clothes and abuses him; Krishna strikes off his head and takes the garments.
source_excerpt: When Krishna asked the king's washerman for fine clothes, the washerman abused him, saying these belonged to the king; and Krishna, angered, struck off his head with his hand, took the garments and distributed them to the cowherds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 31-38)

title: The Weaver and Sudama Honor Krishna
one_line_summary: A weaver dresses Krishna and Balarama, and the garland-maker Sudama honors them and receives a boon.
source_excerpt: A weaver gladly dressed Krishna and Balarama in fine clothes, and Sudama the garland-maker, honoring them with garlands and sandal paste, received from Krishna the boon of unshakable devotion. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 39-51)

title: Krishna Blesses the Hunchback Kubja
one_line_summary: Kubja gives Krishna sandal paste, and he straightens her crooked body into a beautiful woman.
source_excerpt: The hunchback woman Kubja gave Krishna her sandal paste; pleased, Krishna pressed her cheeks and straightened her crooked body into a beautiful woman, and she begged him to come to her house, and he promised. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-12)

title: Krishna Breaks the Great Bow
one_line_summary: Krishna seizes Kamsa's great bow and breaks it, then strikes down the attacking guards.
source_excerpt: Krishna entered the hall of the great bow, seized it though the guards forbade him, and with one hand broke it in the middle like a sugarcane; and with the two pieces he struck down the angry guards Kamsa had sent. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-20)

title: Kamsa Is Terrified by Evil Omens
one_line_summary: Kamsa, hearing of the bow's breaking, spends a sleepless night beset by omens and dreams of death.
source_excerpt: Hearing of the bow's breaking and his guards' death, Kamsa spent a sleepless night terrified by evil omens and dreams — the loss of his own head, visions of corpses, and of himself riding an ass — all foretelling his death. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 25-30)

title: Kamsa Orders the Wrestling Festival
one_line_summary: At dawn Kamsa orders the wrestling festival; the arena is prepared and the cowherds arrive with offerings.
source_excerpt: At dawn Kamsa ordered the wrestling festival, and the arena was prepared with drums and banners; Chanura, Mushtika and the other wrestlers took their places, and Nanda and the cowherds, summoned, arrived with their offerings. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 31-37)

title: Krishna Slays the Kuvalayapida Elephant
one_line_summary: At the arena gate Krishna evades the elephant Kuvalayapida, throws it down, tears out its tusk and slays it.
source_excerpt: At the arena gate stood the elephant Kuvalayapida; when its keeper drove it at Krishna, he dodged beneath it, seized it by the tail and trunk, threw it down, tore out its tusk, and slew the beast and its keepers. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-15)

title: The Citizens Rejoice in the Arena
one_line_summary: Entering with the tusk as weapon, Krishna delights the people, who recount his deeds as Narayana and Rama.
source_excerpt: Entering the arena with the elephant's tusk as his weapon, Krishna delighted the people, who recounted his deeds to one another, saying these two were Narayana and Rama descended in Vasudeva's house. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 16-30)
notes: Largely the citizens' praise and recounting of Krishna's earlier deeds.

title: Chanura Challenges Krishna and Balarama
one_line_summary: Chanura invites Krishna and Balarama to wrestle; Krishna answers that they are boys, but Chanura insists.
source_excerpt: Chanura addressed Krishna and Balarama, inviting them to wrestle for the king's pleasure; Krishna replied that they were boys and would play with equals, but Chanura urged, 'Fight me, and let Mushtika fight Balarama.' (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 30-39)

title: Krishna and Balarama Slay the Wrestlers
one_line_summary: Despite the women's protest, Krishna slays Chanura and Balarama slays Mushtika, Kuta, Shala and Tośala.
source_excerpt: The women protested the unequal match, but Krishna seized Chanura, whirled him and dashed him to the ground, killing him, while Balarama slew Mushtika, and Rama and Krishna slew Kuta, Shala and Tośala. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-27)

title: Krishna Slays Kamsa
one_line_summary: As Kamsa orders Nanda bound and Vasudeva killed, Krishna leaps onto the dais, seizes and slays him.
source_excerpt: As Kamsa ordered Nanda bound and Vasudeva killed, Krishna, enraged, leapt onto the high dais, seized Kamsa by the hair, hurled him into the arena and fell upon him, dragging his body about before all the people. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 28-38)

title: Balarama Slays Kamsa's Brothers
one_line_summary: Kamsa's eight brothers rush at Krishna in fury and Balarama slays them all with his club.
source_excerpt: Kamsa's eight brothers, Kanka and Nyagrodha and the rest, rushed at Krishna in fury, and Balarama slew them all with his club, like a lion among cattle. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 39-40)

title: Kamsa's Wives Lament and Krishna Performs the Rites
one_line_summary: The wives of the slain warriors weep, and Krishna comforts them and has the funeral rites performed.
source_excerpt: The wives of the slain warriors wept and lamented their husbands, and Krishna comforted the royal women and had the customary funeral rites performed for the dead. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 41-48)

title: Krishna Frees Vasudeva and Devaki
one_line_summary: Krishna and Balarama release their parents from bonds and bow, touching their feet.
source_excerpt: Krishna and Balarama released Vasudeva and Devaki from their bonds and bowed, touching their feet; and the parents, knowing their sons to be the lords of the world, embraced them without fear. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 49-50)

title: Krishna Begs His Parents' Forgiveness
one_line_summary: Krishna humbly begs Vasudeva and Devaki's forgiveness for having been unable to serve them.
source_excerpt: Krishna, bowing to his parents, begged their forgiveness that he and Balarama, prevented by Kamsa, had not been able to serve them in their childhood, and could not repay the debt owed to parents. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-8)

title: Krishna Installs Ugrasena as King
one_line_summary: Krishna makes his grandfather Ugrasena king of the Yadavas, honoring Yayati's curse.
source_excerpt: Krishna installed his maternal grandfather Ugrasena as king of the Yadavas, declaring that because of Yayati's curse no Yadava should sit on the throne, and that while he served, the gods themselves would pay tribute. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 11-13)

title: Krishna Restores the Yadava Kinsmen
one_line_summary: Krishna brings back and settles all the Yadava kinsmen who had fled in fear of Kamsa.
source_excerpt: Krishna brought back all the Yadava, Vrishni, Andhaka and Madhu kinsmen who had fled in fear of Kamsa, settled them in their homes with wealth, and they rejoiced daily at the sight of his face. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 14-17)

title: Nanda Departs for Vraja
one_line_summary: Krishna embraces Nanda, bids him return to Vraja, and Nanda departs in tears with the cowherds.
source_excerpt: Krishna embraced Nanda, told him to return to Vraja, and promised to come and see his kinsfolk; and Nanda, his eyes full of tears, departed with the cowherds. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 19-24)

title: Krishna and Balarama Study Under Sandipani
one_line_summary: The two brothers are initiated and go to the teacher Sandipani, mastering all arts in sixty-four days.
source_excerpt: Vasudeva had Krishna and Balarama initiated by the brahmins, and the two, who know all knowledge, went as students to the teacher Sandipani in Avanti, and in sixty-four days mastered all the arts and sciences. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 25-35)
notes: Post-Kamsa Mathura period; no canonical arc covers the gurukula episode, hence 'other'.

title: Krishna Retrieves Sandipani's Son
one_line_summary: As teacher's fee, Krishna slays Panchajana, takes his conch, and brings Sandipani's dead son back from Yama's city.
source_excerpt: As his teacher's fee, Sandipani asked for his son, who had been lost in the ocean at Prabhasa; Krishna slew the demon Panchajana, took his conch-shell body, and going to Yama's city, blew the conch and brought back the boy. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 36-46)

title: Krishna Sends Uddhava to Vrindavan
one_line_summary: Krishna charges Uddhava with a message to console Nanda, Yashoda and the pining gopis.
source_excerpt: Krishna sent his beloved devotee Uddhava to Vrindavan with a message to console Nanda, Yashoda and the gopis, who were pining in his absence. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 1-6)

title: Uddhava Arrives in Vrindavan and Nanda Longs for Krishna
one_line_summary: Uddhava reaches Vrindavan at dusk, is honored by Nanda, who asks after Krishna and remembers his deeds.
source_excerpt: Uddhava arrived in Vrindavan at dusk, was embraced by Nanda and honored as Vasudeva himself, and Nanda, recounting Krishna's deeds, asked after his son; and Yashoda wept as she listened. (rendered from Sanskrit, verses 7-28)
notes: Uddhava's subsequent philosophical discourse (46.29-48) is excluded as pure teaching.
